title: K1814 rerun at the corrected DM bandwidth

claude_followup.brief:
K1814 reran at the corrected HAC bandwidth (aea1646fb: lag = max(h-1, ceil(h^(1/3) n^(1/3))), 24/41/67 for h=1/5/22 instead of 0/4/21). Three things remain, and the first is the one that matters.

1. VERIFY THE DIRECTION HELD. Before the rerun, every h=1 loss-differential acf(1) was positive or near zero, so the prediction is that every |t| SHRANK and the null verdict got more conservative. Check that against the new K1814_results.json: verdict.horizons_with_dl_win must still be empty and verdict.H1_short_horizon must still be FAIL_TO_REJECT. If any horizon now shows dl_beats_both_baselines true, STOP -- that contradicts the pre-measured direction and means something other than the bandwidth changed. Do not publish it, report it.

2. RE-RENDER THE README. Run experiments/k1814/render_readme_results.py so the prose and tables quote the new numbers. Do not hand-edit README.md -- it is generated, and the whole point of this repair is that the artifact is the code's output. The renderer already documents that nested models (harl/ar1/ridge_lags) reach the reader as QLIKE levels only, never as a p-value.

3. RE-CERTIFY. experiments/k1814/review_verdict.json pins a stage-3 PASS against a sha that the bandwidth fix has drifted. That is the designed behaviour, not an obstacle: a verdict is only worth the snapshot it reviewed. Regenerate the template with 'uv run python scripts/experiment_gates.py verdict-template --path experiments/k1814 --out experiments/k1814/review_verdict.json' and commission a fresh review against the new bytes. Note in the brief that an independent review (agy) already passed the METHODOLOGY of the fix on 2026-08-05; what needs certifying now is the rerun output, not the decision to floor the bandwidth. Codex quota is exhausted until 08-08, so use agy or a code-reviewer fallback and record which one in the verdict.

Context: CLAUDE.md methodology rules (K1655) and docs/error_log.md 2026-08-04.
